sources.citation: Smith, R. L. (1985). Maximum likelihood estimation in a class of nonregular cases. Biometrika 72(1), 67–90.
sources.verified: Publisher metadata and abstract; full original proof not accessible. Endpoint exponent alpha and its three thresholds verified against the abstract. Do not cite this as a checked complete proof for Tukey lambda or for uniformity.

sources.citation: Bücher, A. and Segers, J. (2017). On the maximum likelihood estimator for the Generalized Extreme-Value distribution. Extremes 20, 839–872.
sources.verified: Read Propositions 2.1, 3.2, 3.3; discussion 'The role of uniformity'; Appendix C. Three-parameter GEV DQM iff xi > -1/2; normal MLE theorem has compact-set interior assumptions. The authors identify a uniformity gap in Smith's proof; this matters for transferring its claims.

sources.citation: Grimshaw, S. D. (1993). Computing maximum likelihood estimates for the generalized Pareto distribution. Technometrics 35(2), 185–191.
sources.verified: Original seven-page article, especially p.186: its shape k equals -xi here and its scale alpha equals sigma here. Its asymptotic covariance agrees with the inverse of the report's independently derived Fisher matrix. OCR corrupts formulas; the report does not reproduce OCR equations.

sources.citation: Dachian, S., Kordzakhia, N., Kutoyants, Yu. A. and Novikov, A. (2017 preprint). Estimation of Cusp Location of Stochastic Processes: a Survey. arXiv:1711.03740.
sources.verified: Section 1.1 and Remark 1 explicitly discuss the i.i.d. generalized Gaussian example and exponent below 1/2; normalized likelihood is exponential of fractional Brownian motion with power drift. Main displayed example uses an odd cusp, so the report independently derives the even-cusp covariance. The survey explicitly calls its likelihood calculation heuristic.

sources.citation: Prakasa Rao, B. L. S. (1968). Estimation of the Location of the Cusp of a Continuous Density. Annals of Mathematical Statistics 39(1), 76–87.
sources.verified: Identity verified through the survey and DOI citation records. Original DOI endpoint inaccessible; original theorem and assumptions not independently read. Report does not represent this as a verified original proof.

sources.citation: Zhu, D. and Zinde-Walsh, V. (2007). Properties and Estimation of Asymmetric Exponential Power Distribution. McGill working paper dated October 23, 2007.
sources.verified: Read full-text Proposition 5 (printed pp.11–12) and Appendix C: stated location-estimated asymptotic-normality theorem requires both exponents >1. The nearby information-equality sentence must not be used to justify an ordinary Hessian for GED exponent <=1. Final article identity verified separately, but final proof not read.

sources.citation: Zhu, D. and Zinde-Walsh, V. (2009). Properties and estimation of asymmetric exponential power distribution. Journal of Econometrics 148(1), 86–99.
sources.verified: Publisher identity and abstract verified. Institutional copy of final article returned HTTP 502; theorem references in this report refer explicitly to the accessible 2007 preprint.

sources.citation: John, S. (1982). The three-parameter two-piece normal family of distributions and its fitting. Communications in Statistics — Theory and Methods 11(8), 879–885.
sources.verified: Publisher identity and abstract only; the report proves DQM and information rank independently rather than treating the abstract as a theorem verification.

sources.citation: Daniels, H. E. (1961). The asymptotic efficiency of a maximum likelihood estimator. Proceedings of the Fourth Berkeley Symposium, vol.1, 151–163.
sources.verified: Original opening page and conditions visible in search index; direct PDF fetch forbidden. Establishes historical treatment of Laplace's zero a.e. Hessian, not a newly verified full theorem.

sources.citation: Williamson, J. A. (1984). A note on the proof by H. E. Daniels of the asymptotic efficiency of a maximum likelihood estimator. Biometrika 71(3), 651–653.
sources.verified: Publisher metadata and abstract: corrected preliminary result. Do not present the uncorrected Daniels argument as a checked complete proof.
